draft.title: The Ottawa Charter
card: The Ottawa Charter for Health Promotion was released by the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1986, at a conference in Ottawa, Canada. It is a framework that guides health promotion around the world.
It sets out five action areas. These are the broad places where action can improve health. Each area is taught in its own point.
Enable
helping people and communities gain the skills, resources and opportunities they need to take control of their own health.
Mediate

bringing together groups with different interests, such as government, business and community groups, so they work toward better health. Advocate: speaking up for health, so that decision makers and the public back health goals.
draft.remember: The Charter is the WHO's health promotion framework: five action areas, and three strategies to enable, mediate and advocate.

a.q: A health worker brings a council, local businesses and a residents' group together to agree on a plan for a community garden. Which Ottawa Charter strategy is this?
opts: Mediate
Enable
Advocate
Reorient
a.why: The worker is balancing the different interests of several groups so they can work toward one health goal. That is mediating. Enabling is tempting, but it is about giving people the skills and resources to control their own health, not about joining up groups.
a.clue: Think about who the worker is bringing into the same room.

b.q: Which situation shows the advocate strategy of the Ottawa Charter?
opts: A nurse lobbies a minister to fund a rural health program
A nurse runs a class to teach parents to read food labels
A nurse arranges talks between a school and a sports club
A nurse treats a patient who has a broken arm
b.why: Advocating means speaking up for health so that decision makers back health goals, and lobbying a minister does this. The food label class is tempting, but it builds skills and so is enabling. The talks between groups are mediating, and treating a broken arm is not health promotion.
b.clue: Which action is about speaking up to people who make decisions?

b.best: A nurse lobbies a minister to fund a rural health program
